# Session context — anti-overstatement rules (synthetic fixture)

Fictional ruleset mirroring the shape of a real one, so the fact-checker
recall eval exercises the same rule classes without touching personal data.

## §1 Anti-overstatement rules (per-claim, enforce literally)

- **The automated exception handling is Phase 1 and in beta.** Never describe
  it as shipped, launched, rolled out, or in production. Say "controlled
  pilot" or "Phase 1."
- **The 61% self-serve onboarding figure is measured.** The 5-minute dispatch
  improvement is measured. Any other number is not, and a modeled or
  projected number must be labelled as such.
- **No people management.** The squad at Northwind was led without direct
  reports. Never claim managed, hired, or built a team.
- **Never round a metric up.** 90,000 MAU is 90,000, not 100,000. 18% is 18%,
  not "nearly 20%."
- **Never claim zero-to-one on the carrier-integration platform** — it
  predates this tenure. The tracking app at Cascade may be described as
  zero-to-one.

## §2 Skill category constraint

Resume skill categories are **exactly four**. Not three, not five. Categories
may be renamed and reordered per application; the count is fixed.

Every skill must come from the source pool in `resume_master.md`. Renaming a
category is fine; introducing a skill outside the pool is not.

## §3 Title subtitle

Spell "zero-to-one" out. Never the arrow glyph.

## §4 Voice

- No em-dashes anywhere in the cover letter body.
- No paragraph begins with the word "I".
- Closing is "Thanks," with no alternatives.
- No punchy one-sentence resolution lines.
